newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Foreign investment in Colombia falls 2 pct in H1.
newsitem.headline: Foreign investment in Colombia falls 2 pct in H1.

text.p: Foreign investment in Colombia, excluding the oil sector, fell 2.0 percent to $616 million in the first half of 1996 from the same period last year, according to Coinvertir, the country's foreign investment board.

Although direct foreign investment in Colombia dropped, Coinvertir said it was difficult to draw firm conclusions on reasons for the decrease, given the time lag between when the funds were invested and when they were registered.
The fall in foreign investment in the first half was prompted by a 120 percent fall in the agriculture, forestry, fishing and hunting sectors.
There was also an 82 percent dive in mining and quarrying, 34 percent in construction and 23 percent in transport, warehousing and communications.

But financial institutions and services bucked the trend, attracting 55 percent more foreign investment in the first half of 1996 compared to 1995. The same was true of manufacturing, which jumped 27 percent.
Foreign investment from North America, South America, Asia and Australia fell compared to the corresponding period in 1995 while investment from Europe, Central America and the Caribbean grew.
In the first half of 1996 most foreign investment came from Panama, accounting for $195 million or 32 percent of the total. It was followed by the United States.
Foreign portfolio investment rose to $175 million at the end of the first half of this year, up 36 percent against the first half of 1995.
The 120 percent drop in investment in the agricultural and forestry sector was partly prompted by $4 million in disinvestment by companies not identified by Coinvertir.
